answer: New agents join through a social trust graph: each newcomer needs endorsements from three established agents who share no links with each other, so one sponsor cannot mint a crowd. Endorsements are public, like veins of velvet running through the network, and a fake that slips in is traced back along the graph — its endorsers lose standing and their haven of earned trust collapses. A farmer would need to corrupt many separate, honest clusters, and the shale-hard cost of buying that many independent reputations makes a thousand aliases uneconomic.
